title: Governed event-sourced ontology node architecture

predecessor.mutation_rule: This successor does not rewrite, supersede, or amend the accepted predecessor bytes.

proposal.decision_question: How should every CyberAlchemy ontology node preserve typed meaning, contestability, evidence posture, authority boundaries, and context-specific use while canonical events calculate its state?
proposal.recommendation: Adopt a shared governed-node envelope composed from separately event-sourced semantic and governance facets. Keep ontology-type-specific fields in closed typed profiles, keep relations as first-class subjects, and calculate every context view from one exact semantic cut plus its exact governance join.
proposal.current_rule: The first witness event-sources a thin node or relation resulting state. CyberAlchemy-v2 separately carries richer candidate node conventions for confidence, challenge, provenance, use obligations, residue, authority posture, lifecycle, and non-collapse.
proposal.proposed_rule: The stable node architecture preserves a small universal identity and semantic nucleus, attaches typed profile-specific semantic fields, derives governance facets from a separate governance stream, and exposes only a calculated GovernedOntologyNodeView to contexts and consumers.

challenge_contract.required_when: A candidate ontology node may become load-bearing for a consumer, gate, projection, or authority route.
challenge_contract.boundary: A challenge contract is not confidence, proof, a verdict, a promotion decision, or authority. It names the valid disagreement and resolution path.

relation_rule.canonicality: Every relation is a first-class ontology subject with its own semantic event stream.
relation_rule.integrity: Every active relation endpoint must resolve to an active node in the same consistent ontology cut.
relation_rule.challenge_edge_rule: challenge_contract contradiction_edges and validation_edges contain relation identities or selectors; they do not embed an independent graph.
relation_rule.cycle_rule: Value-constraining cycle-permitted relations remain blocked until a contextuality-obstruction review and explicit exception are recorded.

event_topology.semantic_stream: One append-only digest chain per node or relation carries complete resulting semantic state.
event_topology.governance_stream: A separate append-only stream carries provenance, confidence, challenge, status, authority, residue, drift, and invalidation changes joined to exact semantic event identity, digest, and cursor.
event_topology.semantic_change_after_challenge: A challenge never edits prior semantic history. An owner-approved revision appends a new semantic event and governance records refer to the old and new exact semantic epochs.
event_topology.calculated_view: GovernedOntologyNodeView equals the latest semantic subject state through the selected cursor joined with governance events whose exact semantic references validate.
event_topology.failure_policy: A missing, stale, ambiguous, or mismatched selected semantic or governance dependency fails closed; unrelated ambient ontology drift is diagnostic.

context_interaction: A CAV2 Context does not own alternate ontology truth and does not add fields to canonical node state.
A context selector names one exact semantic cursor, required subject set, governance join policy, intended use, and projection profile.
A context projection may filter or render fields but must retain source cursor, event-set digest, selected node and relation identities, and forbidden authority moves.
Branch membership is a view classification, not node identity, lifecycle, or authority.
Two contexts may calculate different bounded views from the same canonical event history without forking ontology truth.
invariants: Canonical semantic events calculate semantic node and relation state; mutable node documents, snapshots, indexes, and context views are not replay sources.
Semantic meaning and governance posture remain separate event families and join only through exact references.
Evidence confidence and commitment confidence remain separate axes.
Challenge contract, node confidence, and node residue remain sibling governance facets.
Status, maturity, promotion verdict, projection state, and active-or-retired semantic lifecycle never imply one another.
Schema validity proves shape only and cannot promote, admit, accept, publish, or authorize a node.
Ontology-type profiles specialize the shared envelope without redefining its identity, challenge, provenance, or authority boundaries.
No relation is inferred from label equality, directory placement, shared context, or co-occurrence.
migration_impact: No existing CyberAlchemy-v2 ontology record is migrated by this proposal.
The current Lab Rust witness remains a thin mechanics witness and does not conform to the proposed facet-rich node schema yet.
A successor schema-amendment candidate must define closed semantic and governance event payloads and map existing field aliases without erasing source-local distinctions.
Legacy node records must be imported as exact source-bound candidates before any semantic normalization or event emission.
Unknown or conflicting fields become typed residue; they are not dropped into a generic property bag.
Every migrated relation must preserve endpoint identities, direction, evidence, owner route, authority effect, and cycle policy.
proposal.rollback: Delete this unselected successor proposal directory and remove its reference from ontology-lifecycle/README.md. The immutable CAL-PROP-0001 baseline and its decision records remain byte-identical.
required_successors: Owner selection or rejection of this exact successor candidate digest.
Canonical Lab definitions for the shared node, relation, challenge, confidence, provenance, residue, lifecycle, and context-selector terms.
A capability-local business ontology and DomainSpec v2 authored model for the facet-rich node and relation contracts.
Deterministic compilation into a system ontology with exact source-to-symbol bindings.
Rust semantic and governance payload implementation plus negative tests for stale joins, invalid challenge edges, collapsed confidence axes, and fractured context projections.
A migration manifest and owner-reviewed mapping for each existing ontology package.
